title: Which Font is Best for Signage?
description: When it comes to creating impactful signage, there's more to consider than just the design and message.
content:
When it comes to creating impactful signage, there's more to consider than just the design and message. One crucial aspect often overlooked is the choice of font. At Herts Signs, your trusted signage manufacturer Hertfordshire, we understand the importance of selecting the right font for your signs. Let's dive into the world of typography and discover which fonts work best for signage printing and design services in Hertfordshire.

1. Legibility is Key

The primary purpose of any sign is to convey a message clearly and effectively. Hence, legibility is paramount. Opt for fonts that are easy to read from a distance. Simple, sans-serif fonts like Arial and Helvetica are excellent choices for this purpose. They offer a clean and modern look, making your message instantly accessible to passersby.

2. Consider the Environment

The environment where your signage will be displayed matters. For outdoor signs, you need fonts that can withstand the elements and remain visible in various weather conditions. Bold and thick fonts, such as Impact or Futura, work well in outdoor settings, ensuring your message remains prominent even in adverse weather.

3. Reflect Your Brand

Your signage should be an extension of your brand identity. The font you choose should align with your brand's personality and values. For a law firm or a financial institution, a classic and formal font like Times New Roman or Baskerville may be appropriate. In contrast, a creative agency might opt for a more playful and unique font like Comic Sans to showcase their creativity.

4. Avoid Overly Decorative Fonts

While decorative fonts can be visually appealing, they often sacrifice legibility. It's best to avoid overly ornate or cursive fonts, especially for signage that needs to convey important information quickly. These fonts can confuse viewers and detract from the message you want to communicate.

5. Maintain Consistency

If you have multiple signs, it's essential to maintain font consistency. Consistency not only reinforces your brand identity but also makes it easier for people to recognize your signage. Stick to a select few fonts that align with your brand and use them consistently across all your signage.

6. Test Before Printing

Before finalising your signage design, it's crucial to test how your chosen font looks in the actual size and format. What appears clear on a computer screen may not translate the same way on a sign. Make sure your font choice remains legible and visually appealing in the real-world context.

Your restaurant's menu is one of the most critical marketing tools you have. Design visually appealing menu boards that showcase your signature dishes, specials, and prices. title: What is screen printing? a step-by-step guide
description: Screen printing is a classic technique where ink is pressed through a stenciled mesh onto a substrate to create printed designs.
content:
Over the years, various industries have utilized printing techniques to add images or text to products. Two popular methods are screen printing and pad printing.

Screen printing is the process of pressing ink through a stenciled mesh screen to create designs. This versatile technique, also known as serigraphy or silk screen printing, is widely used and may have appeared on items you’ve encountered in your daily life.

For those interested in screen printing in Hertfordshire, this article offers a comprehensive guide to the process, including a detailed step-by-step breakdown.

Step-by-step guide to screen printing

Here’s a step-by-step guide to the screen printing process used by Herts Signs:

Step 1: Design Drafting

Begin with your original design or text. At Herts Signs, we print this design onto a transparent acetate film, which will be used to create the screen.

Step 2: Select and Prepare the Mesh Screen

Select a mesh screen appropriate for the material and complexity of your design. We then coat the screen with a light-sensitive emulsion layer to prepare it for exposure.

Step 3: Expose the Emulsion to Light

Place the acetate sheet with the design onto the mesh screen and expose them to bright light. This step hardens the emulsion, creating a precise stencil. For multi-color designs, Herts Signs uses separate screens for each color.

Step 4: Prepare the Stencil

After exposure, wash away the unhardened emulsion to reveal your design on the screen. We ensure the screen is thoroughly dried before moving to the next step.

Step 5: Set Up for Printing

Mount the prepared screen on our printing press, securing it with screws. Depending on the job’s requirements, we use either manual or automatic presses. For complex, multi-color prints, our automatic presses are the preferred choice. We then position the material or fabric on the printing board beneath the screen.

Step 6: Print the Design

Lower the screen to the material and apply ink. Using a squeegee, we press the ink through the screen to transfer the design onto the substrate. For multiple items, we repeat this process by placing new materials under the screen.

Step 7: Heat-Cure and Finish

Dry the printed ink thoroughly with our drying equipment. After drying, we inspect the final product for any residue. The screen is then cleaned with chemicals and prepared for future use.

This process at Herts Signs ensures high-quality and durable results for all your screen printing needs.

Commonly Used Materials in Herts Signs' Screen Printing
